# Components

A catalog file names a component with `{use: <name>, …options}`; EMPAIA converters and publishers are picked by `type:` instead. A component's kind decides where it may be named, and its folder under `src/components/` says the same. To write one, see [Write a component](../guides/write-a-component.md).

| Kind | Usable in | Folder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [loader](#loaders) | served model `weights:`, analysis step `weights:` | `src/components/loaders/` |
| [runtime](#runtimes) | served model `runtime:` | `src/components/runtimes/` |
| [step](#steps) | served model `pre:`, served model `post:`, analysis `steps:` | `src/components/steps/` |
| [source](#sources) | analysis `source:` | `src/components/sources/` |
| [sink](#sinks) | analysis `sinks:` | `src/components/sinks/` |
| [converter](#converters) | EMPAIA exposure `inputs:` | `src/components/empaia/converters/` |
| [publisher](#publishers) | EMPAIA exposure `outputs:` | `src/components/empaia/publishers/` |

## Loaders

Fetches a model's weights (an MLflow artifact, a Hugging Face repo, ...).

Used under a served model's `weights:` and under the `weights:` of an
analysis step that carries its own small model.

### `huggingface` (loader)

Downloads one commit of a Hugging Face Hub repository.

`weights: {use: huggingface, repo: paige-ai/Virchow2, revision: <commit>}`.
The files go to the Hub's own cache (`HF_HOME`), which each deployment
environment points at a shared volume, so a restart downloads nothing.
A gated repository needs `HF_TOKEN` in the environment.

- **Usable in:** served model `weights:`, analysis step `weights:`
- **Example:** `{use: huggingface, repo: paige-ai/Virchow2, revision: 3158645804b69e3f3bc4439d4116edddf0840a72}`
- **Used in:** [`prov-gigapath`](served-models.md#prov-gigapath), [`virchow2`](served-models.md#virchow2)
- **Code:** [`src/components/loaders/huggingface.py`](../../src/components/loaders/huggingface.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repo` | string | required | The repository ID, `<owner>/<name>`, e.g. `paige-ai/Virchow2`. |
| `revision` | string | required | The full 40-character commit hash to download. A branch or tag can move, so the weights would change under the same file. |
| `files` | list of string | not set | Glob patterns of the files to download, e.g. `[config.json, model.safetensors]`; left out, the whole repository. |

### `local` (loader)

Weights at a path on the machine running the model, for tests and trials.

`weights: {use: local, path: /data/model.onnx}`. Nothing is downloaded; on
the cluster the path must be on a mounted volume.

- **Usable in:** served model `weights:`, analysis step `weights:`
- **Example:** `{use: local, path: /data/model.onnx}`
- **Used in:** no catalog file yet
- **Code:** [`src/components/loaders/local.py`](../../src/components/loaders/local.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | required | The weights file or directory on the machine running the model. |

### `mlflow` (loader)

Downloads one artifact (e.g. an ONNX file) from MLflow.

`weights: {use: mlflow, uri: "mlflow-artifacts:/65/<run>/artifacts/model.onnx"}`.
The tracking server comes from the environment (`MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`),
which each deployment environment sets once. After the download the
revision carries the artifact's SHA-256, so `describe()` names the bytes
that run; `sha256:` pins them.

- **Usable in:** served model `weights:`, analysis step `weights:`
- **Example:** `{use: mlflow, uri: 'mlflow-artifacts:/0/0123456789abcdef/artifacts/model.onnx'}`
- **Used in:** [`episeg-1`](served-models.md#episeg-1), [`prostate-classifier-1`](served-models.md#prostate-classifier-1)
- **Code:** [`src/components/loaders/mlflow.py`](../../src/components/loaders/mlflow.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `uri` | string | required | The artifact's URI, e.g. `mlflow-artifacts:/<experiment>/<run>/artifacts/<path>`; it names one run's file. |
| `sha256` | string | not set | The artifact's SHA-256 (`sha256sum` of the file). A run's artifact can be overwritten under the same URI; with this set, a download with other bytes is refused and the analysis runner checks it. |

## Runtimes

Runs a model's weights (ONNX Runtime, timm, ...) inside a served model.

### `onnx` (runtime)

Runs an ONNX graph on ONNX Runtime, optionally through TensorRT.

The graph takes the batch as the host gives it (uint8 RGB tiles,
`(N, 3, tile_size, tile_size)`, unless `pre:` changes them) as its first
input and returns its first output. Input and output names are read from
the graph. The TensorRT engine cache lives in the served model's cache
directory, so a changed model never reuses a stale engine.

- **Usable in:** served model `runtime:`
- **Example:** `{use: onnx}`
- **Used in:** [`episeg-1`](served-models.md#episeg-1), [`prostate-classifier-1`](served-models.md#prostate-classifier-1)
- **Code:** [`src/components/runtimes/onnx.py`](../../src/components/runtimes/onnx.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tensorrt` | boolean | `false` | Try TensorRT first, then CUDA, then CPU. The engine is built on the first start and cached; `describe()` shows which provider is active. |
| `workspace_gib` | number > 0 | `8` | GPU memory TensorRT may use to choose kernels; too little rules out the fast ones for large tiles. |
| `optimization_level` | integer ≥ 0, ≤ 5 | `1` | TensorRT builder optimisation level: higher builds slower and may run faster. |
| `fp16` | boolean | `true` | Let TensorRT use FP16 kernels. |
| `apply_session_options` | boolean | `true` | Give the session `threads`, all graph optimisations and sequential execution. `false` leaves ONNX Runtime's defaults (intra-op threads for every core). |
| `threads` | integer ≥ 1 | `1` | ONNX Runtime's intra-op threads. |
| `output_dtype` | `float32` or `float16` | not set | Cast the graph's output to this dtype, e.g. `float16` to halve a score map; left out, the output keeps the graph's dtype. |

### `timm` (runtime)

Runs a timm model on PyTorch, on the GPU when there is one.

`runtime: {use: timm, num_classes: 0, mlp_layer: swiglu_packed, act_layer:
silu, autocast: fp16, transform: pretrained}` reproduces Virchow2. The
weights are a folder laid out like a Hugging Face repository
(`config.json` and the weights file), as the `huggingface` loader fetches
it; timm reads the architecture and its arguments from `config.json`.

With `transform: pretrained` the runtime takes uint8 RGB tiles and
transforms each one; with `transform: none` it takes the float batch that
`pre:` steps produced. The output is the model's, as float32.

- **Usable in:** served model `runtime:`
- **Example:** `{use: timm}`
- **Used in:** [`prov-gigapath`](served-models.md#prov-gigapath), [`virchow2`](served-models.md#virchow2)
- **Code:** [`src/components/runtimes/timm.py`](../../src/components/runtimes/timm.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `num_classes` | integer ≥ 0 | not set | Classifier outputs, passed to timm's constructor; 0 removes the head, so the model returns its features. Left out, the folder's config decides. |
| `mlp_layer` | `swiglu_packed` | not set | The MLP block, passed to timm's constructor: `swiglu_packed` (timm's SwiGLUPacked, as Virchow2 needs). Left out, timm's default. |
| `act_layer` | `silu` | not set | The activation, passed to timm's constructor: `silu` (torch's SiLU). Left out, timm's default. |
| `autocast` | `fp16` or `none` | `none` | `fp16` runs the forward pass under autocast: float16 on a GPU, bfloat16 on CPU, which has no float16 autocast. `none` runs float32. |
| `transform` | `pretrained` or `none` | `none` | `pretrained` applies the transform timm derives from the folder's config (resize, crop, normalise) to each uint8 tile. `none` passes the batch as given, e.g. as `pre:` steps left it. |

## Steps

Transforms data, row for row.

The same step can be a served model's `pre:` or `post:` or an analysis
step; the catalog file decides where it runs.

### `center_crop` (step)

Keeps the centre square of each uint8 tile, as torchvision's `CenterCrop`.

`pre: [{use: center_crop, size: 224}]` keeps the centre 224 px. An odd
margin puts the extra pixel where torchvision does (it rounds half to
even), and a tile smaller than `size` is padded with zeros first, also as
torchvision does.

- **Usable in:** served model `pre:`, served model `post:`, analysis `steps:`
- **Example:** `{use: center_crop, size: 224}`
- **Reads:** `tile` `uint8[3,?,?]`
- **Adds:** `tile` `uint8[3,size,size]`
- **Used in:** [`prov-gigapath`](served-models.md#prov-gigapath)
- **Code:** [`src/components/steps/center_crop.py`](../../src/components/steps/center_crop.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | integer > 0 | required | The edge of the centre square kept, in pixels. |

### `cls_mean_pool` (step)

Pools a ViT's tokens into two vectors: the class token and the patch mean.

`post: [{use: cls_mean_pool, registers: 4}]` turns Virchow2's tokens
`(1 + registers + patches, dim)` into `(2, dim)`, the summaries
`[global, local_mean]`. It runs in the served model, so only the two
vectors leave the replica.

The mean is computed with PyTorch, the way the encoder's own code pools,
so the features match it bit for bit; PyTorch must be installed where
the step runs. A caller that skips pooling gets the class token and the
patch tokens, without the registers.

- **Usable in:** served model `pre:`, served model `post:`, analysis `steps:`
- **Example:** `{use: cls_mean_pool, registers: 4}`
- **Reads:** `output` `float32[?,?]`
- **Adds:** `output` `float32[2,?]`
- **Used in:** [`virchow2`](served-models.md#virchow2)
- **Code:** [`src/components/steps/cls_mean_pool.py`](../../src/components/steps/cls_mean_pool.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registers` | integer ≥ 0 | `0` | Register tokens after the class token, left out of the mean and of unpooled tokens (Virchow2 has 4). |

### `normalize` (step)

Turns uint8 RGB tiles into the float32 input most PyTorch models expect.

`pre: [{use: normalize, preset: imagenet}]` divides by 255, subtracts the
mean and divides by the std per channel, as torchvision's `ToTensor`
followed by `Normalize` does, and with the same float32 arithmetic, so
the result matches it bit for bit.

- **Usable in:** served model `pre:`, served model `post:`, analysis `steps:`
- **Example:** `{use: normalize, preset: imagenet}`
- **Reads:** `tile` `uint8[3,?,?]`
- **Adds:** `tile` `float32[3,?,?]`
- **Used in:** [`prov-gigapath`](served-models.md#prov-gigapath)
- **Code:** [`src/components/steps/normalize.py`](../../src/components/steps/normalize.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | `imagenet` | not set | Named mean and std: `imagenet` is mean (0.485, 0.456, 0.406), std (0.229, 0.224, 0.225). Give either this or `mean` and `std`. |
| `mean` | [number, number, number] | not set | Per-channel (RGB) mean, on the [0, 1] scale. |
| `std` | [number, number, number] | not set | Per-channel (RGB) standard deviation, on the [0, 1] scale. |

### `resize` (step)

Resizes uint8 RGB tiles, as torchvision's `Resize` does to a PIL image.

`pre: [{use: resize, size: 256, interpolation: bicubic}]` scales a 224 px
tile to 256 px, as Prov-GigaPath's transform does. Pillow does the
resampling, with its antialiasing, so the pixels match torchvision's bit
for bit; Pillow must be installed where the step runs.

- **Usable in:** served model `pre:`, served model `post:`, analysis `steps:`
- **Example:** `{use: resize, size: 256, interpolation: bicubic}`
- **Reads:** `tile` `uint8[3,?,?]`
- **Adds:** `tile` `uint8[3,?,?]`
- **Used in:** [`prov-gigapath`](served-models.md#prov-gigapath)
- **Code:** [`src/components/steps/resize.py`](../../src/components/steps/resize.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | integer > 0 | required | The shorter edge after resizing, in pixels; the longer edge keeps the aspect ratio, so a square tile becomes `size` x `size`. |
| `interpolation` | `bilinear` or `bicubic` or `nearest` | `bilinear` | The resampling filter: `bilinear`, `bicubic` or `nearest`. |

## Sources

Produces an analysis's items from its inputs, e.g. tiles of a slide.

A source whose options include `tile_size` and `mpp` takes its tile
geometry from the analysis's first model step wherever the file leaves
them out; the catalog fills them in when the analysis loads.

### `slide_tiles` (source)

Grid tiles of one slide level, without background or tiles outside the ROI.

Every grid position is a key, so skipped tiles still count toward
progress. The grid covers at least one tile, even on a slide smaller
than a tile.

- **Usable in:** analysis `source:`
- **Example:** `{use: slide_tiles, tile_size: 64, mpp: 0.5, skip_background: false}`
- **Inputs (example options):** `slide` (required), `region_of_interest` (optional)
- **Frame:** `extent_x` `int64`, `extent_y` `int64`, `tile_extent_x` `int64`, `tile_extent_y` `int64`, `stride_x` `int64`, `stride_y` `int64`, `level` `int64`, `mpp_x` `float64`, `mpp_y` `float64`, `downsample` `float64`
- **Adds:** `tile_x` `int64`, `tile_y` `int64`, `tile` `uint8[3,tile_size,tile_size]`
- **Used in:** [`episeg-heatmap`](analyses.md#episeg-heatmap), [`prostate-heatmap`](analyses.md#prostate-heatmap), [`prov-gigapath-embeddings`](analyses.md#prov-gigapath-embeddings), [`virchow2-embeddings`](analyses.md#virchow2-embeddings)
- **Code:** [`src/components/sources/slide_tiles.py`](../../src/components/sources/slide_tiles.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tile_size` | integer > 0 | not set | Tile edge in pixels; the first model step's when left out. |
| `mpp` | number > 0 | not set | Microns per pixel to read at (the closest slide level); the first model step's when left out. |
| `region_of_interest` | `required` or `optional` or `ignored` | `optional` | Whether a run must give a region-of-interest mask (`required`), may (`optional`) or may not (`ignored`); only tiles the mask covers are read. |
| `stride_fraction` | number ≥ 0.05, ≤ 1 | `0.5` | **Per run.** How far apart tiles are, as a share of the tile size: from 0.05 up to 1. 1 places tiles side by side; 0.5 overlaps them by half, for a finer result that takes about four times as long. |
| `skip_background` | boolean | `true` | **Per run.** Whether tiles without tissue are skipped; they get no result. Skipping is faster and leaves empty glass out. On by default. |
| `min_tissue_fraction` | number ≥ 0, < 1 | `0.0` | **Per run.** How much of a tile must be tissue for it to be analysed, when background is skipped: from 0 up to but not including 1. 0 analyses every tile with any tissue; 0.5 needs at least half. |

## Sinks

Writes a run's results into a file of one data format.

### `embedding_table` (sink)

Writes each tile's `features` and position as a row of an embedding table.

Writes `<output>.h5` in the `embedding_table` format: tile corners on the
level read and float32 features, one vector per summary of the served
model, rows in grid order. Tiles the source skipped get no row; when it
skipped all of them, the table is empty.

- **Usable in:** analysis `sinks:`
- **Example:** `{use: embedding_table, output: embeddings}`
- **Reads:** `tile_x` `int64`, `tile_y` `int64`, `features` `float32[...]`
- **Writes:** [`embedding_table`](formats.md#embedding_table)
- **Frame fields read:** `downsample`, `extent_x`, `extent_y`, `level`, `mpp_x`, `mpp_y`, `stride_x`, `tile_extent_x`
- **Rows in order:** yes
- **Used in:** [`prov-gigapath-embeddings`](analyses.md#prov-gigapath-embeddings), [`virchow2-embeddings`](analyses.md#virchow2-embeddings)
- **Code:** [`src/components/sinks/embedding_table.py`](../../src/components/sinks/embedding_table.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `output` | string | required | The output name callers and exposure refer to. |

### `score_grid` (sink)

Averages each tile's `scores` over the cells the tile covers into a score grid.

Writes `<output>.npz` in the `score_grid` format: float32 scores in 0..1
of shape (channels, rows, columns), with which cells any tile covered.

- **Usable in:** analysis `sinks:`
- **Example:** `{use: score_grid, output: heatmap}`
- **Reads:** `tile_x` `int64`, `tile_y` `int64`, `scores` `float32[?,?,?]`
- **Writes:** [`score_grid`](formats.md#score_grid)
- **Frame fields read:** `extent_x`, `extent_y`, `level`, `mpp_x`, `mpp_y`, `stride_x`, `stride_y`, `tile_extent_x`, `tile_extent_y`
- **Rows in order:** no
- **Used in:** [`episeg-heatmap`](analyses.md#episeg-heatmap), [`prostate-heatmap`](analyses.md#prostate-heatmap)
- **Code:** [`src/components/sinks/score_grid.py`](../../src/components/sinks/score_grid.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `output` | string | required | The output name callers and exposure refer to. |

## Converters

Converts one EMPAIA input type (`wsi`, `rectangle`, ...) into a run input.

The analysis's `expose.empaia` declares each input's type, and that type
picks the converter, so nothing is guessed from the data. A converter
contributes the input's EAD io entry and materialises it for a run: a
file in the attempt's workspace, or a value read at admission.

### `primitive` (converter)

An analysis setting offered as an EMPAIA primitive input in standalone mode.

Its type and description come from the setting; the user's value is
read when the job is admitted and overrides the file's.

- **Usable in:** EMPAIA exposure `inputs:`
- **Example:** `{inputs: {<name>: {type: primitive}}}`
- **EAD input type:** `primitive`
- **Gives:** a value
- **Used in:** no catalog file yet
- **Code:** [`src/components/empaia/converters/primitive.py`](../../src/components/empaia/converters/primitive.py)

### `rectangle` (converter)

A rectangle on the app's slide, given to the analysis as a region-of-interest mask.

The rectangle, clipped to the slide, becomes a pyramidal 8-bit TIFF of
the slide's size and pixel size: 255 inside, 0 outside. EMPAIA offers it
with the region-of-interest class, so the viewer lets a user draw it.

- **Usable in:** EMPAIA exposure `inputs:`
- **Example:** `{inputs: {<name>: {type: rectangle}}}`
- **EAD input type:** `rectangle`
- **Gives:** a file
- **Used in:** [`prostate-heatmap`](analyses.md#prostate-heatmap)
- **Code:** [`src/components/empaia/converters/rectangle.py`](../../src/components/empaia/converters/rectangle.py)

### `wsi` (converter)

A slide input: the file it is stored as, linked under its own name.

The RationAI direct-access route names the file on the slide volume,
which model-service mounts where the installation's CDS does. A MIRAX
`.mrxs` comes with its data directory. A slide the route has no path for
is refused: model-service does not download slides.

- **Usable in:** EMPAIA exposure `inputs:`
- **Example:** `{inputs: {<name>: {type: wsi}}}`
- **EAD input type:** `wsi`
- **Gives:** a file
- **Used in:** [`prostate-heatmap`](analyses.md#prostate-heatmap)
- **Code:** [`src/components/empaia/converters/wsi.py`](../../src/components/empaia/converters/wsi.py)

## Publishers

Publishes a stored output of one data format as an EMPAIA output type.

The analysis's `expose.empaia` names the EAD type of each output; the
publisher that reads the sink's format and emits that type is picked.

### `continuous_pixelmap` (publisher)

Publishes a one-channel score grid as a continuous pixelmap on the app's slide.

The SDK builds the pyramid from the grid: exactly what the model produced,
in every slide level from the one it was computed at to the coarsest that
keeps `MIN_PIXELS_PER_SCORE` pixels per score. Tiles are dense, so an
unscored cell inside an uploaded tile reads 0, but a tile without a
scored cell is not uploaded. EMPAIA pixelmaps carry one channel here, so
a multi-channel grid is refused when the analysis loads.

- **Usable in:** EMPAIA exposure `outputs:`
- **Example:** `{outputs: {<output>: {type: continuous_pixelmap}}}`
- **Reads:** [`score_grid`](formats.md#score_grid)
- **EAD output types:** `continuous_pixelmap`
- **Used in:** [`prostate-heatmap`](analyses.md#prostate-heatmap)
- **Code:** [`src/components/empaia/publishers/continuous_pixelmap.py`](../../src/components/empaia/publishers/continuous_pixelmap.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | string | required | The EAD output type to publish as, e.g. `continuous_pixelmap`. |
| `tile_size` | integer ≥ 256, ≤ 2048 | `512` | Pixelmap tile edge in pixels. |

### `primitive` (publisher)

Posts one scalar as the primitive type the analysis names.

The value must fit the type: a bool is not an integer, a float takes
whole numbers, and an empty string is refused. It is checked before
anything is posted.

- **Usable in:** EMPAIA exposure `outputs:`
- **Example:** `{outputs: {<output>: {type: float}}}`
- **Reads:** [`value`](formats.md#value)
- **EAD output types:** `bool`, `float`, `integer`, `string`
- **Used in:** no catalog file yet
- **Code:** [`src/components/empaia/publishers/primitive.py`](../../src/components/empaia/publishers/primitive.py)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | string | required | The EAD output type to publish as, e.g. `continuous_pixelmap`. |
